The gate judges the FORM of every ledger subject and reds when a post-boundary subject is a bare integer, because a bare integer names an issue to a human reader and NOTHING to a machine -- the strict form is `#<n>`. This store exists because a subject is IDENTITY: `docs/instruments/ledger.md` section 9.2 (#52 clause 1) makes a published row immutable, so a malformed subject's repair space is EMPTY -- the repair is a NEW row, and the ORIGINAL still fires forever. Section 9.6 names excusing as the remedy for exactly this shape. THE ADMISSION RULE: every entry names ONE row and carries a `reason` stating which issue number the bare subject named and why the row cannot be repaired in place -- an exemption nobody can check is forgiveness, and this list is debt. An entry that names a row whose subject is NOT a bare integer is a STALE exemption and a gate ERROR, so the store can only ever hold rows that are actually red. Every matched entry prints as an `excused:` line on EVERY run and is counted in the population line, so 'clean' and 'excused' are never the same output. A malformed or duplicated entry, or an unparseable store, is an ERROR. Absent or empty means no exemptions, never a failure.
